subject: food-technology
title: Cold, Drying and Canning
welcome_lead: Three time-tested ways to lock food away from spoilage.
meta_desc: A-Level Food Tech: freezing, dehydration, canning.
final_note: Take away water, heat or both.

concepts.def: Below -18 °C — slows microbial activity, doesn't kill spores.
Fast freezing producing small ice crystals (better texture).
Removing water to lower aw below growth threshold.
Lyophilisation — sublimation under vacuum (premium coffee, drugs).
Sealed container heated to commercial sterility (Appert 1809).
Thermal process ensuring 12D reduction of C. botulinum spores.

walkthroughs.body_html: Domestic freezer at -18 °C halts most spoilage and microbial growth but does not sterilise. Quick freezing (blast, plate, cryogenic) produces small crystals and preserves cell structure better.
Lowering aw below ~0.6 inhibits all microbial growth. Methods: sun drying, drum drying, spray drying (milk powder), freeze-drying for premium products and pharmaceuticals.
Nicolas Appert demonstrated canning in 1809. Modern low-acid canning targets a 12D reduction of Clostridium botulinum — the spore-forming anaerobe responsible for botulism.
